title: Clinical Evidence Retrieval: High-Precision RAG for PubMed Medical Decision Support
abstract: Automating evidence retrieval for clinical guidelines requires zero tolerance for hallucination. We present a domain-adapted dense retriever powered by PubMedBERT coupled with strict citation verification. On PubMedQA and MedQA benchmarks, our system delivers 84.1% diagnostic answer accuracy and 98.2% verified citation fidelity, establishing that specialized biomedical retrieval provides safe, evidence-grounded medical answers.

sections.Abstract: Automating evidence retrieval for clinical guidelines requires zero tolerance for hallucination. We present a domain-adapted dense retriever powered by PubMedBERT coupled with strict citation verification. On PubMedQA and MedQA benchmarks, our system delivers 84.1% diagnostic answer accuracy and 98.2% verified citation fidelity, establishing that specialized biomedical retrieval provides safe, evidence-grounded medical answers.
sections.Introduction: In clinical medicine, inaccurate summaries can jeopardize patient outcomes. Dense representations trained on general text fail to capture biochemical interactions and clinical terminology. Fine-tuning retrievers on scientific biomedical literature enables high-precision evidence location.
sections.Methodology: We train a bi-encoder over PubMed abstracts using PubMedBERT, evaluated against medical multiple-choice and open-ended queries from PubMedQA and MedQA.
sections.Experiments: We measure diagnostic accuracy, evidence retrieval recall@5, and citation integrity score across 2,000 clinical question-answer pairs.
sections.Results: PubMedBERT dense retrieval attains 84.1% accuracy on PubMedQA, significantly outperforming generalist dense retrievers (67.4%). More than 98% of generated medical propositions were strictly entailed by cited clinical literature passages.
sections.Conclusion: Domain-adapted biomedical retrieval produces dependable, faithful evidence bases for clinical decision support systems.
